A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Temp-R1 and contain 20 readable pages, Figures 1–10, Tables 1–13, and Appendices A–E. Their content can be reliably matched. The appendices have identical text and rendered pages.

before.justification: v1 reports original Temp-R1 benchmark results, component ablations, training dynamics, and reasoning-trajectory analyses in Section 5, Tables 2–4, and Figures 4–10.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Temp-R1 benchmark results, ablations, training analyses, and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same action space, rollout procedure, masked supervised cold start, GRPO objective, correctness reward, and reverse curriculum. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions train on MultiTQ and TimelineKGQA-Cron and evaluate on those benchmarks plus TimelineKGQA-ICEWS-Actor. The task categories and out-of-domain scenario are unchanged, as are Appendix A and Table 5.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same baseline rows and comparison coverage, including the same missing RTQA results for ICEWS-Actor. Appendix B's baseline descriptions and Appendix D's cost comparators are unchanged.

E3.justification: The Hits@1 metric, dataset splits, backbone configurations, approximately 1,000 SFT trajectories, and use of 9% of MultiTQ for RL are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same training settings.

E4.justification: The component ablations, backbone comparisons, training-strategy analyses, action-transition analyses, efficiency comparisons, and six appendix case studies are retained without changes to the questions tested or evidence presented.

E5.justification: No run counts, seed details, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added or revised. The point-score tables and training-curve reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Section 5.2 changes Temp-R1's ICEWS-Actor overall score from 0.610 to 0.642. Table 2 already reports 0.642 in both versions, with PoK unchanged at 0.602. This corrects a prose–table inconsistency rather than demonstrating a new performance gain; the other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The TKG and TKGQA definitions, MDP formulation, action-space definition, SFT and GRPO objectives, and curriculum equation are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the autonomous RL-agent contribution, expanded reasoning actions, reverse curriculum, state-of-the-art overall-performance claim, and claimed 19.8% improvement on complex questions. The introduction's replacement of 'comprehensive superiority' with 'superior overall performance' refines wording around an already stated overall-performance claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning cognitive overload, shortcut learning, generalization, and adaptive reasoning remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning models above 8B and the unverified applicability of reverse curriculum beyond temporal reasoning.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code access from a promised future release to stated present availability at the same repository. This is a change in reported availability; the PDFs do not independently verify access. Implementation details, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds eight background references and corresponding introduction citations concerning knowledge graphs, structured reasoning, and agents, including Chen (2024), Liu et al. (2026), and Guo et al. (2026). Section 2 and the substantive positioning against existing TKGQA approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited abstract and introduction wording edits and adds an acknowledgements paragraph naming funding and institutional support. The section order, methodological exposition, experimental narrative, and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: The additions cause limited text and bibliography reflow, including moving the SFT loss equation from PDF page 4 to page 5. Figures and tables retain their content, numbering, captions, and display designs; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the Section 5.2 inconsistency by aligning the ICEWS-Actor score with Table 2 and updates the information about code availability. These provide small gains in reporting consistency and reproducibility information. The method, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
